structure.overview: This case involves Lemay Co Inc. challenging the Minister of Canada's refusal to allow upward adjustments to previously claimed Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS) amounts. Lemay applied for judicial review after the Minister denied their request to amend claims for certain periods, citing statutory interpretation issues under the Income Tax Act (ITA). The Federal Court dismissed the respondent's motion to strike, finding Lemay's judicial review application has a reasonable chance of success and that no internal recourse exists, allowing the case to proceed to a merits hearing.

sections.label: Respondent's motion to strike and legal standards
Legal standards for motion to strike
Statutory interpretation arguments on CEWS claims

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court dismisses the motion to strike, finding the respondent failed to prove the judicial review application is doomed or that internal recourse exists.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Minister audited and found Lemay overclaimed CEWS by $311,204 for periods 6,7,13-15 and underclaimed for periods 8-12 due to a calculation error.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On March 27, 2023, the Minister notified Lemay of intended assessment and adjustments for periods 6,7 and 13-15 where overclaiming occurred.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On May 12, 2023, Lemay requested the Minister to use discretion under ITA subsection 125.7(16) to increase claims for periods 8 to 12 by $1,715,341.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On June 22, 2023, the Minister confirmed adjustments for overclaimed periods but refused Lemay's upward claim for periods 8 to 12, citing CRA technical interpretation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On July 26, 2023, Lemay submitted additional arguments citing ITA provisions allowing the Minister to grant higher CEWS amounts for periods 8 to 12.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On September 11, 2023, the Minister again refused Lemay's claim, stating no jurisdiction to allow upward adjustments beyond original timely claims.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On October 11, 2023, Lemay applied for judicial review of the Minister's refusal decision.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On October 25, 2023, the respondent informally suggested reconsidering subsection 125.7(16) analysis, contrary to the Minister's official refusal.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Lemay rejected the informal reconsideration since the official refusal letter remains the enforceable decision under review.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The respondent moved to strike, arguing Lemay's interpretation is doomed and internal recourse under subsection 125.7(16) must be exhausted first.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Applications should not be struck before merits hearing except in exceptional cases where no possibility of success exists.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The party moving to strike must meet a stringent standard proving the application should be struck.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: When statutory interpretation is involved, the court must find if the applicant's interpretation has a reasonable chance of success before striking.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court should not make definitive legal rulings on competing statutory interpretations on a motion to strike, only assess reasonable prospects.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The respondent argues ITA 125.7(5)(a) prohibits paying subsidies exceeding the originally claimed amount, making Lemay's claim doomed.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Lemay contends 125.7(5) limits overpayments but does not bar amending original CEWS applications to correct errors.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Lemay claims the Minister has inherent power under ITA subsections 152(3.4) and 164(1)(b) to allow new returns, opposing respondent's view.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Lemay's argument on ITA 164(1)(b) and 152(3.4) was rejected by the Minister and is central to the judicial review application.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The respondent argues subsection 152(3.4) only remedies overpayment timing and does not permit upward adjustments to original applications.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The respondent views subsection 152(3.4) as unambiguous and subject to the limitation in subsection 125.7(5).

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The respondent did not rebut Lemay's argument on paragraph 164(1)(b); subsection 152(4) does not fully address Lemay's position.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Considering ITA subsections 125.7(5), 152(3.4), and paragraph 164(1)(b), it is unclear if the Minister can reject amended forms as Lemay requests.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On a motion to strike, the court cannot definitively interpret ITA provisions when multiple reasonable interpretations exist.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The respondent failed to prove it is plain and obvious that Lemay's interpretation allowing amended forms has no reasonable chance of success.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Minister has already ruled that subsection 125.7(16) does not allow Lemay's claim, negating internal recourse.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Lemay requested subsection 125.7(16) discretion on May 12, 2023; the Minister refused on June 22, 2023, citing CRA's internal interpretation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Minister determined no recourse exists under subsection 125.7(16) and rejected the application, contrary to respondent's claim.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On September 11, 2023, the Minister reiterated subsection 125.7(16) allows original applications but not amendments to prior claims.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The respondent now argues the Minister's interpretation is erroneous and that internal recourse under subsection 125.7(16) does exist.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes the respondent's interpretation of subsection 125.7(16) ITA is plausible but the Minister rejected it in the judicial review decision.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states the Minister's decision means there is no internal and effective recourse available to Lemay under subsection 125.7(16) ITA.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects the respondent's argument that internal recourse exists since the Minister already decided otherwise; Lemay had to file judicial review.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court says deciding the Minister's interpretation and jurisdiction is for the trial judge at hearing, not on a motion to strike without full submissions.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court concludes the respondent cannot object to the Minister's conclusions on a motion to strike and order Lemay to submit a prohibited application.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court extends the time limits under Federal Courts Rules by 30 days from the decision date as requested by the respondent.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court orders costs of $3,285 payable to Lemay as agreed by the parties.
